label: Consequentialism
description: Evaluating acts or other objects through their consequences.

label: Special obligations
description: Duties arising from relationships, commitments, or roles rather than duties owed identically to everyone.

label: Aggregation
description: Combining benefits and burdens across people when evaluating options.

label: Moral luck
description: The influence of factors beyond an agent's control on moral assessment.

label: Virtue ethics
description: An approach that gives moral character and practical judgment a central explanatory role.

label: Consent
description: Authorization through agreement, with questions about understanding, capacity, and freedom from pressure.

label: Beneficence
description: Reasons or duties to benefit others and prevent harm.

label: Intergenerational ethics
description: Duties and fairness involving people who live at different times.

label: Moral status
description: The basis and extent of a being's claim to moral consideration.

label: Restorative justice
description: Responses to wrongdoing focused on addressing harms, accountability, and relationships.

label: Care ethics
description: Ethical attention to dependency, relationships, and situated responsibilities of care.

label: Moral responsibility
description: Conditions under which conduct and consequences are appropriately attributed to an agent.

label: Deontology
description: Ethical approaches that give duties, permissions, or constraints a foundational role.

label: Intrinsic value
description: Value something has in itself, distinguished from its usefulness as a means.

label: Moral relativism
description: Accounts relating moral truth or justification to standards of cultures or other frameworks.

label: Repentance
description: Acknowledgment of wrongdoing joined to a changed orientation and questions of repair.

label: Moral uncertainty
description: Uncertainty about which moral principles or judgments are correct.

label: Instrumental rationality
description: Assessment of means relative to an end, distinct from justification of that end.

label: Bodily autonomy
description: Authority over one's body and limits on others' interference.

label: Reflective equilibrium
description: Mutual adjustment of judgments, principles, and background commitments in pursuit of considered coherence.

label: Truth and belief
description: The distinction between holding a claim and the claim's being true.

label: Testimony
description: Acquiring belief or knowledge through what others communicate.

label: Epistemic luck
description: Accidental correctness that raises doubts about whether a true belief counts as knowledge.

label: Peer disagreement
description: Disagreement among people of comparable relevant competence and access to evidence.

label: Epistemic rationality
description: Standards for beliefs and inquiry as directed toward truth or other epistemic goods.

label: Epistemic injustice
description: Wronging someone in their capacity as a knower, including distorted credibility or interpretive exclusion.

label: Negative evidence
description: Absence that counts as evidence when presence would probably have been detected.

label: Regress of justification
description: The challenge of explaining how reasons support beliefs without infinite regress or vicious circularity.

label: Memory knowledge
description: Knowledge or justified belief retained or reconstructed through memory.

label: Epistemic independence
description: The extent to which sources supply information without merely inheriting the same origin.

label: Knowledge how
description: Practical competence and its relation to propositional knowledge.

label: Skepticism
description: Challenges to whether or how knowledge in some domain is possible.

label: Inductive justification
description: Support for conclusions extending beyond observed cases.

label: Expertise
description: Specialized competence relevant to the reliability of judgments within a domain.

label: First person evidence
description: Evidence accessible through one's own experience or perspective.

label: Intellectual humility
description: Recognition and responsible management of the limits of one's epistemic position.

label: Fallibilism
description: The view that knowledge or justification need not require an impossibility of error.

label: Epistemic responsibility
description: Responsibilities governing inquiry, belief formation, and management of uncertainty.

label: Understanding
description: Grasp of explanatory or other significant connections, contrasted with merely possessing isolated information.

label: Epistemic dependence
description: Reliance on other people, institutions, and inherited methods in acquiring knowledge.

label: Modus ponens
description: The valid inference from if P then Q, together with P, to Q.

label: Unstated premises
description: Assumptions an argument needs but does not explicitly state.

label: Validity and truth
description: The distinction between a conclusion being true and following from its premises.

label: Affirming the consequent
description: The invalid general inference from if P then Q and Q to P.

label: Equivocation
description: A shift in a term's meaning that disrupts an argument.

label: Quantification
description: Logical expressions of scope such as some, every, and none.

label: Interpretive charity
description: Interpreting an argument fairly while respecting what its author actually commits to.

label: Circular reasoning
description: Reasoning that relies on the disputed claim in a way that fails to provide the required support.

label: Analogical reasoning
description: Reasoning from relevant similarities between cases.

label: Slippery slope
description: An argument linking an initial step to a sequence of further consequences requiring support.

label: Ad hominem
description: An attack on a speaker that does not appropriately address the support for their claim.

label: False dilemma
description: Treating a restricted set of alternatives as exhaustive without adequate grounds.

label: Necessary conditions
description: A condition that must hold for something, distinguished from a condition that guarantees it.

label: Counterexamples
description: Cases that challenge a general claim by satisfying its scope while violating its conclusion.

label: Burden of proof
description: The responsibility to supply appropriate support for a claim in a context of inquiry.

label: Consistency
description: Compatibility of commitments under the same relevant meanings and circumstances.

label: Inferential strength
description: How strong or broad a conclusion the premises warrant.

label: Abduction
description: Inference toward an explanatory hypothesis, often through comparison with alternatives.

label: Argument revision
description: Changing premises or inferential steps to address an objection without arbitrary exception.

label: Undercutting defeaters
description: Reasons that undermine a source of support without directly establishing the opposite conclusion.

label: Modality
description: Necessity, possibility, and their relation to what is actual.

label: Persistence
description: What it takes for something to continue existing through change.

label: Social ontology
description: The existence and dependence of institutions, roles, obligations, and other social entities.

label: Causation
description: Relations of production, dependence, or difference-making between events or states.

label: Free will
description: Agency and control over action, including their compatibility with determinism.

label: Relations
description: Connections between things and questions about whether these are metaphysically fundamental.

label: Abstract objects
description: Putative entities such as numbers that are not ordinary concrete spatiotemporal objects.

label: Vagueness
description: Borderline cases and indeterminacy in the application of concepts.

label: Cosmological explanation
description: Accounts of the existence or dependence of the universe as a whole.

label: Grounding
description: Non-causal dependence sometimes expressed as one fact obtaining in virtue of another.

label: Identity
description: Being one and the same entity, distinguished from qualitative resemblance.

label: Response dependence
description: Accounts locating some properties in relations to observers or their responses.

label: Natural kinds
description: Categories proposed to track significant divisions in nature rather than mere convenience.

label: Personal identity
description: Conditions for the persistence of a person across time and change.

label: Compatibilism
description: The view that determinism can be compatible with the relevant kind of free agency.

label: Levels of description
description: Different explanatory vocabularies or scales used to describe a phenomenon.

label: Laws of nature
description: General principles of nature and questions about their necessity or governing force.

label: Nothingness
description: The proposed absence of all entities, distinguished from empty space.

label: First cause
description: A proposed explanatory origin or ground that does not itself depend on a prior cause.

label: Ontological parsimony
description: Preference for avoiding unnecessary entities, balanced against explanatory demands.

label: Phenomenal consciousness
description: The felt or experiential character of a conscious state.

label: Other minds
description: The problem of knowing or explaining experience in subjects other than oneself.

label: Artificial understanding
description: Whether and how artificial systems can possess understanding rather than merely produce convincing outputs.

label: Knowledge argument
description: An argument using new experience to challenge the completeness of exclusively physical knowledge.

label: Extended mind
description: The proposal that some cognitive processes extend beyond an individual's biological boundaries.

label: Attention
description: Selective orientation of cognitive resources and its relation to consciousness.

label: Emotion
description: Affective states involving feelings, bodily changes, appraisals, and action tendencies.

label: Embodied cognition
description: Accounts in which bodily capacities and activities help constitute or shape cognition.

label: Mental causation
description: How mental states can contribute causally to actions and other events.

label: Self knowledge
description: Knowledge of one's own mental states, motives, and character.

label: Psychological continuity
description: Connections of memory, intention, disposition, and other psychological features across time.

label: Empathy
description: Understanding or sharing another's affective perspective without assuming identity of subjects.

label: Nonlinguistic thought
description: Cognition that does not require linguistic expression or representation.

label: Homunculus problem
description: An explanatory regress caused by attributing the unexplained capacity to an inner agent.

label: Self conception
description: A person's understanding and interpretation of who they are.

label: Neural explanation
description: Explaining cognition and behavior through processes in the nervous system.

label: Animal consciousness
description: The possibility, nature, and evidence for experience in nonhuman animals.

label: Unity of consciousness
description: The relations through which experiences are presented together or as belonging to one subject.

label: Process self
description: Accounts of the self as an organized continuity of activity rather than an unchanging substance.

label: Explanatory gap
description: The apparent gap between explaining physical or functional processes and explaining felt experience.

label: Procedural justice
description: Fairness in decision procedures, distinguished from fairness of resulting distributions.

label: Political legitimacy
description: The justification of political authority and the right to impose binding rules.

label: Majority rule
description: A collective decision rule that gives the greater number of votes decisive procedural weight.

label: Distributive justice
description: Principles governing the allocation of benefits, opportunities, and burdens.

label: Equality of opportunity
description: Fair access to positions or prospects and the significance of unchosen starting conditions.

label: Non domination
description: Freedom understood as security against arbitrary or uncontrolled power.

label: Freedom of expression
description: Protections for communication and debate and the grounds for legitimate limitations.

label: Civil disobedience
description: Principled breach of law as a form of political contestation.

label: Migration ethics
description: Ethical questions about admission, movement, borders, and duties to displaced people.

label: Public reason
description: Justification of shared political arrangements through reasons others can reasonably assess.

label: Reparative justice
description: Duties to address the consequences of past or continuing injustice.

label: Structural power
description: Power exercised through social arrangements, dependencies, and control of opportunities.

label: Democratic authority
description: The justification and limits of rule through democratic procedures.

label: Emergency powers
description: Exceptional authority claimed in response to serious threats and its required constraints.

label: Collective action
description: Coordination and contribution problems involving shared benefits or costs.

label: Value pluralism
description: The possibility of multiple important values that cannot simply be reduced to one measure.

label: Complicity
description: Responsibility associated with participating in or enabling another's wrongdoing.

label: Prioritarianism
description: Giving additional moral weight to benefits for those who are worse off.

label: Associational freedom
description: Freedom to form, join, leave, and maintain associations and the limits of their authority.

label: Epistemic democracy
description: Accounts connecting democratic participation to the quality of collective inquiry or decisions.

label: Aesthetic judgment
description: Evaluative judgment about beauty or other aesthetic qualities.

label: Reasons for taste
description: Considerations offered to support or criticize aesthetic appreciation.

label: Authenticity
description: Relations between a work's identity, origin, history, and claims to genuineness.

label: Ethical criticism of art
description: The relation between a work's moral features and its artistic or aesthetic value.

label: Definition of art
description: Accounts of what makes something art, distinct from whether it is good art.

label: Authorial intention
description: The creator's intended meaning and its relevance to interpretation.

label: Aesthetic emotion
description: Emotional experience elicited through engagement with art or aesthetic objects.

label: Environmental aesthetics
description: Aesthetic appreciation of natural and human-shaped environments.

label: Cultural appropriation
description: Borrowing cultural practices and the importance of power, attribution, and context.

label: Creativity
description: Production or recognition of something novel and valuable in a relevant practice.

label: Artistic value
description: The kinds of merit a work may have as art.

label: Ontology of art
description: The nature and identity conditions of artworks, performances, and copies.

label: Aesthetic cognition
description: Relations between knowledge, interpretation, perception, and aesthetic experience.

label: Originality
description: Novelty or distinctiveness of a contribution in relation to relevant precedents.

label: Public art
description: Art in shared spaces and its civic, expressive, and institutional roles.

label: Aesthetic expertise
description: Informed competence in perceiving, interpreting, and evaluating aesthetic objects.

label: Expression
description: How works or acts articulate feelings, attitudes, or perspectives.

label: Conservation
description: Preservation and restoration of works, including tensions among material, appearance, and history.

label: The sublime and the beautiful
description: Contrasting aesthetic experiences of beauty, overwhelming magnitude, disturbance, or power.

label: Canon formation
description: Processes through which institutions and communities select works as exemplary or enduring.

label: Confirmation
description: The evidential support observations can provide for a hypothesis.

label: Underdetermination
description: The possibility that evidence leaves more than one theoretical account available.

label: Causal inference
description: Reasoning about what produces or changes an outcome rather than merely correlates with it.

label: Scientific models
description: Representations used to investigate systems, often through deliberate simplification.

label: Falsifiability
description: A claim's exposure to possible empirical refutation.

label: Scientific realism
description: Commitment to some theory-described entities or structures as mind-independent realities.

label: Operationalization
description: Connecting a theoretical construct to procedures for observing or measuring it.

label: Replication
description: Repeating or independently reproducing an investigation to examine the stability of a finding.

label: Values in science
description: Roles of epistemic and social values in research choices and judgments.

label: Scientific change
description: Changes in theories, concepts, or standards over the history of inquiry.

label: External validity
description: The extent to which findings transfer beyond the conditions or population studied.

label: Emergence
description: System-level properties arising through organization or interaction among components.

label: Selection bias
description: Distortion arising when inclusion in observed data is related to the quantity or comparison of interest.

label: Prediction and explanation
description: The relation between forecasting outcomes and accounting for why they occur.

label: Statistical inference
description: Drawing conclusions from data using probabilistic methods and their assumptions.

label: Measurement uncertainty
description: Limits on the precision and interpretation of measurements and estimates.

label: Theory ladenness
description: Influence of conceptual and theoretical commitments on observation and interpretation.

label: Simulation
description: Computational representations of systems whose implementation and empirical adequacy require separate checks.

label: Explanatory pluralism
description: The use of multiple legitimate explanatory approaches for different aspects or aims.

label: Construct validity
description: The evidential basis for interpreting and using a measure as representing an intended construct.
